Utterance: Many clinicians can have a lot of uncertainty about the best way to ask about and screen for childhood traumas or adverse childhood experiences. This video models how a clinician can ask about these things in a structured and evidence-based way, even in the context of a routine clinical appointment. The questionnaire being used is called the ACE, or the Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire. It's a 10-item tool that asks about childhood experiences such as sexual, physical, or verbal abuse, physical neglect, and emotional deprivation. It also asks if a child has experienced parent loss due to incarceration or divorce, major mental illness or substance use in a parent, and domestic violence. For each endorsed item, the child gets one point, called their ACE score. We screen for these because a large body of literature links these events with long-term serious physical and mental health outcomes. Higher scores increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, diabetes, depression, substance use, and suicide.
